Heavy rain swept through tents sheltering displaced Palestinians in Gaza City on Saturday, leaving families wading through water around their shelters. The flooding is making daily life increasingly difficult for people in the camps, who are now facing a third winter there. "This is the first day of rain, and of course we are already flooded," said Olfat El-Magdoub, a displaced Palestinian sweeping water from her tent. She said that when it rained two weeks ago she spent four days sleeping on blankets on the floor because the bedding was soaked. Rafiq Ghattas, who lives in the Mina camp, home to around 1,700 families, said conditions deteriorated within an hour of the rain starting. Why is Gaza drowning? Images of floods engulfing Gaza have gone viral. Most coverage focuses on the humanitarian catastrophe. Few explain what caused it. Since October 2023, Israeli forces have destroyed nearly all of Gaza’s infrastructure. Up to 68 million tons of rubble now blanket the Strip. Homes, schools, hospitals, and basic services have been flattened, with at least 90 percent of the territory destroyed. Now, as winter sets in, the first rains are making what is left unlivable. At least five people have been killed after sand embankments collapsed in the downpour. None of this is new. The Israeli plan to make Gaza unlivable has been unfolding for years. In 2012, the UN warned that Gaza could be unlivable by 2020 because of repeated Israeli assaults, a crippling blockade, the collapse of its aquifer, energy shortages, and mass unemployment. Despite the so-called ceasefire, our reporter in Gaza describes a situation that is impossible to endure: no shelter, no aid, and a ban on rebuilding. Conditions are getting worse by the day.” @specter_affairs

This year’s olive harvest has been the most violent in recent memory, with settler attacks on Palestinian farmers reaching a new high. But for Masafer Yatta, this is only the latest escalation in a decades-long campaign by the Israeli state to expel Palestinians from their land by any means necessary. Working in coordination with the army and police, nearby settlers wage a ceaseless battle against the Palestinians living in this area. Professor Ilan Pappé describes what has been happening to Masafer Yatta since the 1970’s as “incremental colonization, ethnic cleansing, and oppression,” and to be here is to see it firsthand. But the people of Masafer Yatta have earned a reputation for themselves for their resistance to state and settler terror. They simply refuse to leave, and the Israelis simply won’t stop trying to force them to. The Nakba never ended. We’re just watching its latest act.

Free Palestine 🇵🇸 Some disagreements are about politics. This one is about whether the killing of children can ever be justified. The actor behind the Hulk speaks about struggling to talk to people who try to justify Israel’s killing of Palestinian children. His frustration raises a question that reaches far beyond Hollywood: how do you keep having a conversation when you feel the other person is defending something fundamentally indefensible? Children do not choose the governments they live under. They do not choose armed groups, military operations or the circumstances into which they are born. Their lives should never be treated as an acceptable price, an inconvenient detail or a footnote in someone’s political argument. You do not need to agree on every part of this conflict’s history to recognise that Palestinian children deserve to grow up. They deserve safety, an education, a family and a future. Their humanity does not depend on whether recognising it is politically convenient. Condemning the killing of Palestinian civilians does not require dismissing the suffering of Israeli civilians. Caring about one child should never depend on caring less about another. The same principle must apply to everyone: civilians must be protected, and the actions of governments and armed groups must be open to scrutiny. Celebrities are often told to stay out of politics. But when the subject is children being killed, speaking out is also a moral choice. So is staying silent. Fame does not make somebody an expert, but you do not need to be an expert to insist that a child’s life has value. The difficult question in this clip is personal: where do you draw the line between respecting someone’s different opinion and refusing to accept what they are defending? At what point does “we just disagree” stop being enough? Could you stay friends with someone who tried to justify the killing of children? 👇 #FreePalestine #Palestine #Gaza #ProtectChildren #HumanRights
